ko.executive_summary: Custom silicon acceleration for AI workloads has shifted from niche to competitive necessity: Google TPUs now distribute via Oracle OCI, Amazon pursues Decart ($7B) to escape NVIDIA inference costs, AWS launches TorchNeuron to erode CUDA lock-in, and Google-led custom chips forecast to outship GPUs by 2028. The interface value has migrated from monolithic GPU dominance to heterogeneous chiplet/HBM stacks with software abstraction layers (PyTorch, Bedrock prompt caching) that decouple workload optimization from hardware vendor.
key_facts: Google TPU integration into Oracle OCI (first-time hyperscaler cross-licensing)
Amazon Decart acquisition target $7B for AWS chip flexibility
Google-led custom AI chips projected outship GPUs by 2028
AWS TorchNeuron releases to commoditize Trainium adoption, counter CUDA moat
SK Hynix SSD controllers with 100+ embedded processors (custom HBM era)
Microsoft Maia 300 AI accelerator shown at OCP 2026
Broadcom AI chip business confirmed booming amid competitive pressure signals
Amazon inference cost thesis: 10x expense premium vs. internal chip target

implications.text: Custom HBM (Samsung, SK Hynix) and chiplet stacks now table-stakes; monolithic GPU memory hierarchy loses margin as hyperscalers standardize on 2.5D/3D packaging with vendor-agnostic controller logic.

PyTorch native support (Google, AWS), Bedrock prompt caching, and TorchNeuron collectively reduce lock-in friction, allowing rapid custom-chip adoption—erosion of NVIDIA's proprietary compiler moat accelerates.

Oracle TPU resale, Amazon Decart bid, Google OCI distribution, and Microsoft Maia 300 roadmap signal 4-way race to own training+inference pipeline; Broadcom remains bottleneck for networking fabric (RDMAoE, InfiniBand).

Amazon's stated 10x inference expense ratio drives bespoke silicon urgency; custom ASICs now table-stakes for >50% model serving volumes, reshaping capex allocation away from general-purpose accelerators.

ko.counterpoint: NVIDIA retains software ecosystem depth (CUDA libraries, optimized frameworks) that custom-chip teams require 12–24 months to replicate; interim-period workload migration risk remains high for latency-sensitive inference at scale.
ko.feasibility_observation: SK Hynix 100+ processor SSD controller and Google-Oracle TPU distribution signal no material design-feasibility blocker for custom silicon, but yield and volume ramp sustainability unclear given hyperscaler fab capacity constraints (Vietnam plant missed 2027 target signals broader foundry capacity squeeze).
ko.change_note: Last week no-change; this week custom-silicon momentum shifted from strategic intent to execution: hyperscaler cross-licensing, CUDA-parity software releases, and cost-driven M&A (Decart) now visible—interface control (packaging, software boundary) shifting away from NVIDIA.

ko.executive_summary: Packaging competitive topology pivots toward geographic supply-chain redundancy and material-layer control rather than node-driven consolidation. Hanmi Semiconductor's U.S. base opening, Amkor's margin gains in advanced packaging, and Intel-AMD chiplet collaboration signals fragment design-at-interface arbitrage further; simultaneously, adhesive localization (Henkel Korea) and interposer heterogeneity (Egis-SiPearl CPU chiplets for Europe) erode single-vendor packaging dominance and raise barriers to technical lock-in at the substrate-protocol boundary.
key_facts: Hanmi Semiconductor opens U.S. manufacturing base; market cap KRW 18.1 trillion
Amkor Q3 2026 results highlight margin expansion in advanced packaging segment
Intel-AMD chiplet collaboration announced, targeting advanced packaging and custom silicon
Egis (Taiwan) partners SiPearl (France) on CPU chiplets for sovereign EU AI infrastructure
Applied Materials doubles Singapore R&D and manufacturing footprint
Henkel establishes Korean factory producing adhesives for AI chip assembly
Yield management solutions market projected US$3.19 billion by 2035

implications.text: Hanmi + Henkel + Applied Materials geographic expansion decouples packaging from traditional Taiwan-Korea duopoly; enables customer lock-in via proximity and adhesive/material supply leverage at substrate layer.

Intel-AMD collaboration and Egis-SiPearl EU partnership signal competing interposer protocols emerging outside TSMC-controlled CoWoS; multiplexes technical interface control to system integrators and reduces single-node dependency.

Adhesive and resist localization (Henkel, dry-deposited resist R&D at KU Leuven/Imec) shifts competitive moat from die-attach to bonding material IP; lower capex barrier than lithography but higher switching cost than commodity flip-chip.

Applied Materials Singapore expansion + Egis-SiPearl CPU chiplets + US helium classification reflect de-risking against China supply friction; packaging becomes geopolitical checkoff, not pure efficiency play.

ko.counterpoint: Material-layer fragmentation (adhesives, resists, interposer variants) may drive test/yield costs up and time-to-volume down if standardization stalls; Amkor margin gains could reverse if substrate commoditization accelerates across multiple regional fabs.
ko.feasibility_observation: Amkor Q3 2026 margin expansion in advanced packaging implies yield/volume ramp visible this cycle; Henkel Korean adhesive factory and Applied Materials Singapore doubling signal confidence in mass-production feasibility for next-gen bonding and equipment supply, though EUV resist tone behavior variance (KU Leuven/Imec) hints at E-beam lithography fine-tuning still required for high-volume RDL.
ko.change_note: Last week emphasized interposer outsourcing (TSMC-GF arbitrage) and node-centric fragmentation; this week's data reveals geographic substrate redundancy and chiplet-protocol multiplexing are operationalizing faster—adhesive and resist localization now visible alongside packaging migration, indicating material IP and system-level integration are overtaking node economics as competitive boundary.

ko.executive_summary: Co-packaged optics (CPO) and silicon photonics are consolidating as critical AI infrastructure interfaces. Nvidia-SPIL's 15x capacity expansion by mid-2027 and Taiwan's LandMark's record Q3 EPS on silicon photonics demand confirm supply-chain lock-in at the optical-electronic boundary; Micro LED variants (Erised, Starksemi, San'an backing) now passing customer validation, signaling technology divergence at the modulation layer. Market estimates of $50B+ reflect mainstream adoption, but competitive pressure concentrates around transceiver density and thermal management at the package edge.
key_facts: Nvidia-SPIL targeting 15x co-packaged optics capacity expansion by mid-2027
LandMark Optoelectronics Q3 EPS NT$6.12 on silicon photonics; capex commitment NT$8 billion
Kyushu University-Sumitomo Chemical achieved 180 Gbaud ultrafast operation on KNN thin-film waveguide modulators
Starksemi Micro LED optical interconnect passed leading customer technical validation
CScale raised $145M for AI optical interconnects; Erised Series B for Micro LED optical links
Optical interconnects market estimated at US$50.09 billion
Schneider Electric 2.5MW power module; Nvidia DSX POD architectural integration
PsiQuantum optical circuit switch for AI data centers; Vuzix entering optical interconnect

implications.text: Nvidia-SPIL duopoly consolidation on CPO capacity through 2027 creates bottleneck at photonic-electronic interface; competing Micro LED paths (Starksemi, Erised, San'an) emerging as alternative transducer architecture to challenge silicon photonics incumbents.

KNN thin-film waveguide (Sumitomo-Kyushu) and Micro LED transducers now achieving 180 Gbaud+ performance parity with standard silicon photonics, fragmenting optical modulation standards at customer validation threshold.

LandMark's NT$8B capex surge and venture funding surge (CScale $145M, Erised Series B) indicate shift from legacy optoelectronics vendors toward specialised AI optical-link designers as primary value accrual node.

Power module scaling (Schneider 2.5MW) and DSX POD architecture tightening power-optical co-location constraints, elevating thermal dissipation and signal-integrity at transceiver interface as differentiator.

ko.counterpoint: South Korea AI spending slowdown risk and NIST quantum-resistant crypto migration timeline (tagged macro) may dampen near-term optical-link capex velocity if end-customer data center builds delay; near-parity performance of Micro LED vs. silicon photonics at 180 Gbaud does not yet confirm yield or cost leadership.
ko.feasibility_observation: Design feasibility for silicon photonics modulation improved: Kyushu-Sumitomo 180 Gbaud KNN waveguide and Starksemi Micro LED both achieving customer-validation milestone, confirming ultrafast operation and thermal efficiency at scale. No mass-production yield gates visibly broken this week, but LandMark's NT$8B capex commitment and CScale-Erised funding indicate fabs and tool suppliers ramping.
ko.change_note: From 'no change' to confirmed CPO supply-chain acceleration: Nvidia-SPIL 15x expansion target, LandMark record revenue, and dual-track modulation architectures (silicon photonics + Micro LED) now validating at customer tier, shifting competitive boundary from research to production-readiness.
